name: Saint Agatha
history: A young Christian of Catania in Sicily who had consecrated her virginity to God and was martyred in the persecution of Decius around 251. Her cult spread quickly through the Church, and her name is said in the Roman Canon. She is patron of Catania and of Malta, and is invoked against fire, the eruptions of Mount Etna and diseases of the breast.
life: Agatha’s story, written down some time after her death, tells of a girl of good family who refused the advances of the governor Quintianus. He handed her over to a woman who kept a brothel, hoping to break her will, but she remained steadfast. She was then imprisoned and cruelly tortured, and her breasts were cut off. Tradition holds that Saint Peter appeared to her in prison and healed her wounds. She died after further torments, praying to Christ who had given her strength. A year after her death, the story goes, Mount Etna erupted, and the people of Catania carried her veil before the lava, which stopped. Saint Gregory the Great dedicated a church to her in Rome that had been taken from the Arians. In paintings she carries her breasts on a dish, and in Sicily small cakes in that shape are still made for her feast.
prayerTo: Saint Agatha, bride of Christ, you kept faith through cruelty and shame, and the Lord healed and crowned you. Pray for all women who are abused or exploited, for those who suffer from cancer, and for me, that I may stand firm in trial and trust Christ to heal what has been wounded. Amen.
penance: Pray today for women who suffer violence and for those with breast cancer. Give to a charity that cares for them, or visit someone who is ill.
meditation: Agatha found strength in Christ when everything was taken from her. What do you have left when your own strength runs out?
prayer: O God, Who among the other miracles of thy power have bestowed the victory of martyrdom even upon the weaker sex, graciously grant that we who commemorate the anniversary of the death of blessed Agatha, thy Virgin and Martyr, may come to thee by the path of her example. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
